subject: Horizon Health — clarification on storage, retention, and audit for prompts/outputs
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + narrow questions on PII retention for prompts/outputs

Hi Elena — great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking through the Horizon Health use case and the examples where you pipe patient notes into our API for summarization and triage. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the important points and surface a few targeted clarifying questions so your security/legal team can confirm whether Redwood's defaults meet Horizon's controls or if we should propose contract-level adjustments.

Short recap (from our discovery):
- Primary flows: patient free-text -> Redwood hosted API (text generation) -> sanitized summary stored in Horizon EHR.
- Concern areas: prompt content retention, generated output retention, audit logs/access logs, and regional residency (must be us-east-1).

Targeted questions for you / your security reviewers:
1) For prompts and model outputs: do you require that raw prompt text or generated output be retained by the vendor for troubleshooting/observability? If so, for how long (e.g., 0d / 30d / 90d / 365d)?
2) Audit/logging window: do you need user-level access logs retained beyond our default enterprise offering (we can provide 365d with add-on)?
3) Residency: confirmed requirement is us-east-1 only — correct?
4) Embeddings/indexing: will you want Redwood to persist embeddings for retrieval, or will Horizon maintain its own vector store?

What I can confirm right now (high level — I’ll get legal/security text for contracts):
- Hosted API default: request and response payloads (prompts + outputs) are retained for up to 30 days for debugging and abuse prevention; they are not used for model training.
- Enterprise customers can: opt to set retention to 0 days for content, or contract for longer retention if you need extended forensic windows.
- Dedicated / Private deployments: retention is managed by the customer; by default Private (on-prem/VPC) does not send content to Redwood control plane unless you activate remote diagnostics.
- Audit logs (auth/access): Redwood stores structured access logs; enterprise SLA includes 365-day retention as an add-on.
- Region selection: hosted data is stored in the region you pick at onboarding (we support us-east-1 / eu-west-1 / ap-southeast-1).
- Caching: in-memory KV/prefix caches used to speed inference are ephemeral (kept in RAM), not written to persistent storage unless you enable cache snapshotting for warm restarts.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short summary (redwood_pii_handling_summary.pdf) and our DPA retention excerpt (redwood_dpa_retention_clauses.txt) for your legal/security teams.

Next step: can you confirm answers to Q1–Q4 above or point me to the person on your team to validate? If useful, we can schedule a 30–45m session including our security engineer and a Redwood legal rep.

Thanks — Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Elena Park <elena.park@horizonhealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security_team@horizonhealth.com
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + narrow questions on PII retention for prompts/outputs

Thanks, Nikhil — helpful summary. A few clarifications from the Horizon security/legal side:

- For regulatory compliance we generally require vendor retention of any data containing PHI to be explicitly defined in contract. Horizon's baseline ask is 0–30 days for content stored by vendors; however, for troubleshooting and incident response we may accept up to 90 days if stored encrypted at rest and access is auditable.
- For auditability, we need immutable access logs (who/when) for at least 365 days. Is that available as a standard export or do you provide a log ingestion integration (S3/Kinesis)?
- Residency: yes, behind a strict control that all data at rest and backups must reside in us-east-1 and be under Horizon-managed keys (we can share KMS details).
- Embeddings: Horizon prefers to control the vector store; we would not want Redwood to persist embeddings on your side.

Can you provide a concise statement we can attach to our vendor review: 1) exactly what is retained by default (fields/payloads), 2) whether Redwood uses any customer data for model training (yes/no), and 3) how long different telemetry types are kept (content, embeddings, access logs, aggregated metrics)? Also please send the DPA/contract snippet with the retention clause.

If possible, schedule the security call tomorrow afternoon (Horizon time).

—Elena
Director, IT Security, Horizon Health

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + narrow questions on PII retention for prompts/outputs

Elena — appreciate the detail. Below is a concise vendor statement you can attach to your review packet; I’ve also attached the short PDF and the DPA snippet we discussed. If you need formal legal language we can flag it for our contracts team, but this should cover the technical controls.

Vendor statement (technical summary):
1) Default content retention (hosted API):
   - Request payloads (prompts) and generated outputs (responses) are retained for up to 30 days by default for debugging, abuse prevention, and support.
   - Content stored for this purpose is encrypted at rest (AES-256), access-controlled, and logged.
   - Customers may request 0-day retention for content to be automatically purged on ingest; this is available as a standard enterprise configuration.
2) Use of data for model training:
   - Redwood does not use customer-provided prompts or outputs to train or fine-tune public models. Any use of customer data for model improvement requires an explicit opt-in and contract term.
3) Embeddings and indexing:
   - Redwood will not persist embeddings for Horizon unless explicitly enabled. If you maintain your own vector store (recommended for your scenario) Redwood will not retain copies.
4) Caching and KV storage: transient in-memory caches (KV caches, attention caches) are ephemeral and do not persist to durable storage unless you enable snapshotting/diagnostics.
5) Audit and access logs:
   - Structured auth/access logs (who/when) are kept by default for 90 days.
   - Enterprise customers can add the 365-day log retention package (we provide daily exports to a customer-owned S3 bucket or Kinesis stream).
6) Regional residency and key management:
   - Hosted data is stored in the selected region (we will provision your tenant in us-east-1).
   - For enterprise customers we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for data at rest. Backups and replicas remain in-region unless otherwise agreed.
7) Encryption and access controls:
   - All content at rest is encrypted; network transport is TLS1.3. Role-based access controls and per-call audit trails are standard.

Attachments included: redwood_pii_handling_summary.pdf (one-page controls summary), redwood_dpa_retention_clauses.txt (DPA excerpt showing configurable retention options), call-notes-20271101.txt (internal call notes).

Next steps I propose:
- Quick 30m security/technical call with our security engineer + your security team to confirm KMS and S3 export details.
- If Horizon requires 0-day retention for prompt content, we can enable that prior to any PII traffic.

Do you want us to provide a DocuSign-ready DPA with the 365-day logs add-on and 0/30/90 configurable retention options?

Thanks — Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>

Hi Elena — looping in from legal/ops side to move this to next steps. Per Nikhil's summary we can:
- Provision your tenant in us-east-1 and enable BYOK KMS during onboarding.
- Offer 0-day content retention as a configuration toggle to prevent any request/response persistence.
- Enable 365-day immutable audit log export to a Horizon-owned S3 bucket (we'll provide the ingestion role).

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll send a DocuSign link today with a DPA that includes the 365-day logs add-on and explicit retention configuration options (0/30/90).
2) Schedule a 30m technical call with our security engineer tomorrow at 11:00 AM ET — does that work for your team?

Quoted for context: "Default content retention (hosted API) ... retained for up to 30 days" (from Nikhil's message).

If you confirm the call time and the S3 bucket details (or preferred log destination), we’ll get the DPA over and lock the tenant region.

Best,
